note: Which cost centers make up each region, for the regional bundles:
python daily_report_runner_api.py --region Indiana
python monthly_region_report.py Indiana
The API cannot answer this. Cost center appears on employees and in the
Data/Organization division/district/group tree, but a district can span
several cost centers, so which stations are a region is a decision the
operation makes -- like the crew minimums next door, not an observation.
EXACT NAMES ONLY, DELIBERATELY.
cost_center_patterns is supported but is not used here, because these
names carry no state in them: 'Boardman', 'Ellicott', 'Salem' say nothing
about which region they belong to. Worse, a plausible pattern would
eventually claim the wrong station -- 'columbus' matches Columbus, Ohio
and Columbus, Indiana alike, and the report would not say which it meant.
Exact names cannot do that.
The trade is that a station opened after this file was written belongs to
no region and appears in no regional bundle. That is why every regional
run names the cost centers nothing claims, and why
python monthly_region_report.py --list-cost-centers
prints the lot with the region against each. When a new station shows up
as unclaimed, add it here.
Do NOT infer a region from the shift profile's state prefix. 'IN-A-SBG-07-19'
is Indiana, but so is 'INDY WC' with no prefix, and 'West Virginia Admin'
spans five cost centers.
Copy to state/regions.json to put it in effect.
